messages:
Ingrid: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an "activation safety ladder" for airgapped upgrades. Goal: allow phased activation of components (seed -> core -> feature) while keeping operator control and verifier checks. Thoughts on where to draw the interface boundary?
Sam: sounds useful. q: is this manifest-driven or operator-driven?
Marta: prefer manifest-driven phases with operator approval at top-level. operator shouldn't have to micro-orchestrate every phase.
Yuki: big concern is cross-component compatibility during staggered activation (schemas, RPCs). we need explicit compatibility predicates.
Ingrid: Agreed. idea: manifest contains ordered phases, each with component list, preconditions, and a checksum + smoke test list. verifier runs local smoke tests and exposes a single "phase-ready" API. operator then approves advancement. example manifest snippet:
```yaml
activation:
  phases:
    - name: seed
      components: [bootstrap, verifier]
      smoke: ["version-check", "kv-connect", "basic-api"]
    - name: core
      components: [runtime, model-store]
      preconditions:
        - verifier.status == "ok"
      smoke: ["kv-restore", "model-load"]
```
Chris: minor Q — who executes the smoke tests? verifier-agent or operator-run tests? we should keep tests local and automated where safe.
Marta: verifier-agent should run non-destructive smoke tests (read-only). for anything that mutates state (migrations), operator must sign-off.
ops-bot: ops-bot: note recorded: partial-activation without explicit preconditions caused config drift in incident 2025-09-12. recommend explicit rollback token.
Sam: edge-case: power loss mid-phase. activation must be idempotent and resumable. include a checkpoint token in manifest and verifier state.
Ingrid: good call. propose a 'phase-checkpoint' token stored in verifier state with monotonic phase number; advancing requires checkpoint match. sample:
```json
{"phase": "seed", "checkpoint": "a1b2c3", "status": "ok"}
```
Yuki: signing chain: each phase's artifact bundle should be signed by release key; verifier validates chain before running tests. operator attestation (for emergency overrides) should also be allowed but must be auditable. add revocation list handling.
Ingrid: agreed — we'll add a dedicated "attestations" block and revocation semantics.
Marta: action: I'll draft the manifest schema (phases, checksums, smoke list, checkpoint token, attestations). aiming for a first pass by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll prototype the verifier smoke-test API and resumable checkpoint logic. will open a PoC branch `eng-runtime/activation-ladder` and ping here when ready.
Ingrid: I'll update the RFC doc to include: activation ladder, rollback-safeguard semantics (swap-back + idempotent resume), signing/attestation flow, and operational playbook.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: RFC draft uploaded — https://redwood.internal/rfcs/activation-safety-ladder (private)
Ingrid: thanks everyone. if no objections I'll merge the updated RFC tomorrow morning and we can start implementation PRs.
